clue.text: They suggest Silver didn't wipe his feet on the mat

definitions.text: They suggest Silver didn't wipe his feet on the mat

parts.words: They suggest Silver didn't wipe his feet on the mat
parts.note: read one way, these are muddy prints left in the entrance passage by a man called Silver; read the other, they are the stamps assayers punch into silver

explanation.walkthrough: The italic Silver looks like a person (Long John, perhaps) tramping across the doormat; the stamps on silver plate certify its purity.
explanation.definitionFit: Assay office stamps on precious metal certify it, and marks on a hallway floor show someone came in with dirty boots.

definitions.meaning: kicks on the shins, as in rugby or football
riding horses for hire

explanation.definitionFit: Kicking an opponent's shins is a foul, and ordinary hired riding nags share the word.

clue.text: Reading Roman Law ? But for Greek I need this

definitions.text: Reading Roman Law ? But for Greek I need this

parts.note: lex is the Latin word for law
to con is to study or pore over

explanation.surface: A student can manage Latin legal texts unaided, but Greek demands a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: Latin law may be read unaided, but to read Greek one needs a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary of an ancient language is the classicist's aid to reading the texts.

definitions.meaning: illicit whisky distilled by night, and the light of the night sky
nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg liquor and the glow from the night sky, plus foolish talk such as rubbish.

parts.note: the Scottish National Party stands for independence; an early champion of that cause won at Bannockburn in 1314

explanation.definitionFit: The fourteenth century king who beat the English at Bannockburn was an early winner for Scottish independence.

indicators.note: the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: feeling rough is feeling ill

explanation.surface: A traveller feels queasy on the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Sic transit gloria mundi, 'thus passes the glory of the world', is the Latin tag; sic means so.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin for thus begins the motto about passing glory, and is used to mean the word is as written.

clue.text: A boot of this shape is barred

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are to be reformed into another shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boot made to some odd pattern is not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of this shape' asks for the letters of A BOOT bent into a new form.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by custom or rule is barred, banned and off limits.

clue.text: 28 bereft of all-round secretary ? What a business !

indicators.note: the letters for the secretary are taken away from 28

parts.note: the answer to 28 across
a typist addressed as Miss, whose letters surround the rest

explanation.surface: Someone is left without a secretary who does everything, and the firm suffers.
explanation.walkthrough: In old offices a typist was addressed as Miss, so 'secretary' gives that title; 'all-round' says it wraps the rest of 28 across, and 'bereft of' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large business combine, such as a cartel, is a trust.

clue.text: Signor of same complexion as the late Captain in Cranford?

definitions.text: Signor of same complexion as the late Captain in Cranford?

parts.words: Signor of same complexion as the late Captain in Cranford?
parts.note: in Mrs Gaskell's novel Cranford the late Captain is Brown; the Italian conjuror's name echoes the Italian for brown

explanation.definitionFit: The conjuror who visits Cranford takes his stage name from bruno, Italian for the captain's surname colour.

clue.text: Yet it might have been right under one's eyes

definitions.text: Yet it might have been right under one's eyes

parts.words: Yet it might have been right under one's eyes
parts.note: a failure to notice, though the word itself suggests something above or within view

explanation.definitionFit: A mistake made by not noticing something is a slip that may have been in plain view.

clue.text: Steersman with set of teeth that's unflattering

definitions.note: the definition describes the word as a name: a disparaging label for a vain man

parts.note: the cox steers a rowing boat
a comb is a row of teeth

explanation.surface: A rowing helmsman with ugly teeth is told so to his face.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the term itself: calling a man a vain fop is no compliment.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a conceited dandy is an insult, so the term is a disparaging epithet.

parts.note: not the salad oil and vinegar but clothing made in Paris by the great fashion houses

explanation.definitionFit: High fashion dressmaking is the craft of the Paris salons, literally dressing in the French manner.

definitions.meaning: dismisses from a job
large bags of coarse cloth hold goods

explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss an employee is to give the push, and coarse bags hold coal or potatoes.

clue.text: Effects of potations going right (and not quietly) to the head

definitions.text: Effects of potations going right (and not quietly) to the head

indicators.note: one letter goes into the word in place of another
says which letter is thrown out: the one for quietly, not kept
places the swap at the front of the word potations

parts.note: taken as written: drinks
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: Strong drink, gulped noisily, goes straight to the drinker's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping R for P at the front of POTATIONS gives the head spins that heavy drinking brings on.
explanation.definitionFit: Too many drinks make the head spin, so turnings round are what the drink does to it.

clue.text: The content of kisses for Peter Pan

definitions.text: The content of kisses for Peter Pan

parts.words: The content of kisses for Peter Pan
parts.note: in Barrie's play Wendy calls a kiss by the name of a sewing cap for the finger, so the content of such kisses is tiny amounts

explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan's 'kisses' are sewing caps, and their content is very small measures.

definitions.meaning: a unit of weight, 2240 pounds in Britain
10 across is high fashion; style or fashionable society, as in bon ..., is what it demands

explanation.walkthrough: The French word for fashionable style gives the second sense; 10 across is the Paris dressmaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A long measure of weight, and fashionable style (the old word for society's elegance) expected of haute couture.

parts.note: a city's bell-ringing announcer pictured as one who weeps

explanation.definitionFit: The official who rang a bell to proclaim news in the streets, with crier read as one who sobs.

parts.note: read as 'what a tiler is doing': laying roof tiles so they overlap, with a nod to Wat Tyler, leader of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt

explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381; spelt 'Wot', the name becomes 'what a tiler' is doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying tiles or scales in overlapping rows is exactly a roofer's work.

parts.note: not an uncle wearing a cloak but an oom, the Dutch-derived word for uncle, living in Cape Province, South Africa

explanation.definitionFit: Boer settlers in the Cape speak a language in which 'oom' is uncle, and are white South Africans of Dutch descent.

clue.text: What's left of the point — the lot ?

definitions.meaning: the digits to the left of a decimal point form an integer
the entire amount, every bit of it

explanation.definitionFit: An integer sits to the left of a decimal point, and 'the whole' amount means everything.

clue.text: Came clean about being a high-rise landlord

definitions.meaning: confessed
possessing property on the upper floors

explanation.definitionFit: Admitting guilt, and literally having title to flats high up.

definitions.meaning: a pet form of Elizabeth
a small gamble

explanation.definitionFit: A short form of Elizabeth, like Liz, and a wager, which a flutter is in British slang.

clue.text: Timothy likely to get stung early

annotationWithheld.clue: Timothy likely to get stung early

clue.text: Chinese tin 14 across, might see after that

indicators.note: places the rearranged letters after what came before

parts.note: a can is a tin
the answer to 14 across, a unit of weight

indicators.note: the word see might be some other arrangement of its letters, so they are mixed

explanation.surface: Chinese tin weighing a ton might come into view afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' is a weak but traditional anagram signal: the word see might be rearranged; 14 across is a cross-reference to that answer, the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The language and people of Canton, a city in southern China, are a Chinese group.

definitions.meaning: the Hollywood film statuette
the first name of Wilde, who wrote the comedy An Ideal Husband

explanation.definitionFit: The Academy statuette, and the forename of Wilde, author of An Ideal Husband.

clue.text: They are rapacious and strung up to test current tendencies

definitions.meaning: birds of prey of the hawk family

definitions.text: strung up to test current tendencies
definitions.meaning: paper toys flown on strings show the wind's direction, and figuratively test opinion

explanation.definitionFit: Hawk-like raptors, and toys on strings which show which way the wind blows, as when floating an idea.

definitions.meaning: opposing groups in a dispute or game
the Dunmow Flitch, a side of bacon, is awarded to a married couple who have not quarrelled for a year

explanation.walkthrough: The Dunmow Flitch, an English custom in Essex, gives a side of bacon to a couple who have not quarrelled for a year and a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing teams are factions, and the flitches of bacon won year after year at Dunmow are halves of a pig.

definitions.meaning: index fingers
in algebra the little raised numbers showing a power

explanation.definitionFit: The pointing finger is the index, and exponents in mathematics express powers.

definitions.meaning: a surface-to-air guided weapon
a man's name, short for Samuel

explanation.definitionFit: A surface-to-air rocket is known by its initials, and a common short form of Samuel.

indicators.note: the shape of the word nun is changed, so its letters are reordered
the word dame is knocked about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun has been transformed and an upset lady will be seen to shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transfigured' turns NUN into UNN and 'distressed' turns DAME into AMED; 'anon' is short for anonymous, not the old word for soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon abbreviates anonymous, which describes something without a name.

definitions.meaning: read as steer's man: a cowboy who lassos young bullocks
climbers are linked by a rope, so whoever ties them together does that job

explanation.walkthrough: After 9 across the solver expects a cox again, but here the steer is a bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowhand lassoes steers with a lariat, and a climbing party is tied together on a line.

clue.text: Won't believe Scotch opacity — is conducive to red influence ,

parts.note: Scotch mist is a thick drizzling fog
corrodes metal with a red coating

explanation.surface: A doubter refuses to believe that Scottish fog makes things go red.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a sentence: damp fog makes iron go red.
explanation.definitionFit: To doubt or suspect someone is to refuse belief in them.
